scope: bounded typed mailboxes of ptr-exec (Mailbox and its cloneable MailboxSender) under overload: capacity never exceeded, ownership preserved (every offered message is delivered or handed back, never lost, duplicated or altered), admission identical to a VecDeque reference queue at every event, and tail latency and memory bounded; latency is gated in virtual ticks of a deterministic discrete-event simulation that uses the real Mailbox for every admission, compared with an unbounded std::sync::mpsc baseline through the same oracle; a threaded arm with real producer threads checks the ownership ledger and the capacity, while its wall-clock latency and resident set are descriptive only
limitations: scope is ptr_exec::Mailbox and MailboxSender only; the RequestAdmission queue, supervision, restart, cancellation and async mailboxes are not covered

latency is virtual: the gate is wait in simulated ticks against the analytic bound capacity x S_max, not wall-clock time; the threaded arm's wall-clock latency and peak resident set are descriptive and never gated

the threaded arm checks exact counts only (every one of thousands of repeated fills admits exactly the capacity, an Ok after a returned close() is a violation, the ledger holds after the join, a closed mailbox returns every value); how the scheduler interleaves producers is not controlled, so its contended-stage totals vary between runs and are only required to show all three outcomes (admitted, Full, Closed)
the model is single-server with uniformly distributed service times and a fixed phase plan; it does not reproduce a real isolate's service distribution, and payload classes differ only in body size
a bounded mailbox that refuses is back-pressure, not delivery: a refused message is returned to the producer, and what the producer does next (retry, shed, escalate) is outside the claim
the reference queue is a VecDeque with a capacity written for this harness; agreement with it shows the Mailbox matches this model, not that the model is the only sound one

negative controls (an unbounded channel, a drop-oldest wrapper) and canaries (duplicating, mutating, lossy, LIFO, capacity+1, capacity x2, early refusal, ignored close, closed reported as empty) show the oracle can tell them from a sound queue; a passing mailbox is the expected outcome

the mutation checker's evidence (results/mutations.json) is about the harness, not the mailbox; COMPLETED requires it (every planned mutation killed) as a precondition of trusting a pass, so without it the verdict is INVALID, and it says nothing about the mailbox itself

wait_bound_violations and payload_bound_violations are corollaries of the capacity, FIFO and model rules and of the harness's own work-conserving consumer (they cannot trip unless those do), and the p99 rule is implied by wait_bound_violations; they are kept because they are the experiment's stated latency and memory claims, not as independent evidence
memory is the queue bound only: the live payload bytes follow from the queue depth; the mailbox's own allocation (the VecDeque buffer) is not gated and appears at most in the descriptive resident set

a panic or a hang of the product is a falsification (product_panics, product_hangs), contained by the harness; a hang is detected only in the threaded arm, by a 20 s watchdog; a panic in harness code itself is a harness fault (INVALID)
timings come from one shared cloud container; no capacity claim
